subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond the existing `messages.suppressToolErrors` boolean, and what safety semantics should it use for failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config and user-visible failed-mutation semantics; source inspection proves the gap, but cannot choose whether operators may hide warnings that currently protect users from silent false success.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep the boolean only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and narrow this issue to docs or specific remaining channel leaks.

options.title: Split narrow leaks first
options.body: Defer the enum and handle channel-specific or tool-class-specific leaks in narrower issues before designing a shared policy.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available routing candidate from recent warning-policy ownership and the merged PR that explicitly left this broader issue open.
